business_type: mature compounder (enterprise software + cloud, currently in an investment supercycle)
moat_source: enterprise switching costs across Office/Windows/Azure identity stack plus Azure scale; evidence: 18% revenue growth at $330B+ annual scale with Azure +40% - but gross margin at its narrowest since 2022 shows the moat funding an arms race

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% of the gap closed by year 3. Excludes dividend (~0.9%/yr).

sensitivity_key_driver: capex peak timing and the FCF-margin recovery slope
primary_model_risk: Twin concentration: the FCF recovery assumes the ~$190B capex cycle peaks in calendar 2026 AND that the ~45% of backlog tied to OpenAI converts to revenue as contracted. Either failing - capex extending or OpenAI faltering - pushes the bear case ($183) to the center. No megacap has ever carried this much single-customer exposure.
expectations_gap_key_variable: OpenAI counterparty risk: the -30% drawdown has already repriced the capex fear; the residual ~16% premium to our expected IV is the market granting more benefit of the doubt on the OpenAI-linked backlog than we do
top_5_bull_arguments: Cheapest megacap AI spender: 22.8x trailing after a -30% drawdown, with Azure still growing 40%
AI run-rate $37B growing +123% - the monetization is real even if Copilot lags
Record $46.7B quarterly operating cash flow; the FCF squeeze is a capex choice, not a demand problem
$625B of contracted backlog provides multi-year revenue visibility unmatched in software
If capex peaks on schedule (bull case), FCF rebuilds to ~$185B by 2030 and the stock re-rates toward $452
top_5_bear_arguments: ~$281B of backlog rides on OpenAI's survival and solvency - a single-counterparty risk with no precedent at this scale
FCF -22% y/y and gross margin at a four-year low while capex guidance keeps climbing
Expected IV ($325) is ~16% below the price even after the worst month in 25 years
Copilot enterprise adoption is the monetization bridge and it is reportedly wobbling
Depreciation from the build-out compounds for years regardless of AI demand outcomes
thesis_breakers: OpenAI distress, renegotiation, or material cancellation within the $281B RPO exposure
CY2027 capex guided above CY2026's ~$190B (no peak)
Azure growth below 30% cc for two consecutive quarters
FCF margin failing to improve sequentially by mid-FY2027
Microsoft 365 Copilot seat growth stalling in enterprise disclosures
position_size_recommendation: 0-2%; the most defensible megacap entry of the AI complex on further weakness - accumulation zone near expected IV (~$325)
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios. Revenue/EPS/Azure/capex/FCF/backlog are reported or management-stated - a strong data foundation; the post-2026 FCF slope is constructed - confidence_level medium.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence. Verified datapoints: -30% from the 52-week high of 555.45, worst month in more than 25 years (June 2026, Motley Fool), +0.45% past week, trailing P/E 22.82 (pass1/search). No verified historical multiple range beyond this captured.
